opening: Lord, meet us gently today and always
body:
This reveals something profound about how God works.

He does not unveil everything at once. He prepares humanity through centuries of prophecy, symbols, covenants, and visions. Moses, Isaiah, Daniel, Ezekiel, and the other prophets each held a piece of the puzzle. Then, in Christ, the entire picture came into focus.

The Transfiguration was another of those moments—a glimpse behind the veil. Peter, James, and John saw what Daniel had only seen in vision: the divine glory of the Son. But Jesus instructed them to remain silent because the story was not complete. Only after the Resurrection could they proclaim not merely that they had seen His glory, but that the crucified Jesus is the glorified Son of Man whom Daniel foresaw.

I think that’s one of Scripture’s most beautiful patterns: God is never late, and He is never hurried. He reveals truth exactly when humanity is able to receive it. Prophecy is not merely prediction; it is God’s patient preparation for the moment when Christ is fully revealed.
